policy: The v1.6.3 contract is frozen: each active source's URL building, list parsing and JD fetch live in jobs_scraper/sources/<source>.py, and sg_product_jobs.py keeps only thin wrappers over them — one implementation per behaviour, verified by AST. The active CLI sources are linkedin, jobstreet, cake and 104/onezerofour; jora stays retired from active crawling and is kept only for back-compat dedup of historical rows. Every source adapter's list fetch retries a transient 429/5xx/connection/JSON failure with a 30/60/90s ladder (four attempts), raises any other 4xx without retrying, and never retries a legitimately empty page; a run counts as successful only when the list crawl actually produced pages, because an empty crawl exits 0 by design. Code that generates a Python worker embeds its arguments as Python literals, never as JSON: json.dumps(None) is the bare token null, an undefined name in Python, and such a worker dies before it reaches Google and silently costs the run the subprocess timeout guard that protects the Sheet write. A generated worker never carries the jobs payload in its source: the payload travels in a separate JSON file the worker reads, because a source that embeds it grows to megabytes and makes CPython pull the whole literal through its tokenizer before the write can start, which is a memory spike on a machine whose free-page count is already in the tens of megabytes. The engine's title filter, Sheet write order, cross-source identity, work-mode values and single-source-of-truth crawl state are unchanged by this release; future source expansion or retirement requires an explicit authorized contract change. Outbound proxy resolution lives in one place, jobs_scraper.sources.resolve_proxies(), and every adapter that talks to a third party uses it: JOBS_SCRAPER_PROXY first, then the standard HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY / ALL_PROXY, and nothing set means a direct connection; no source may reach for a proxy variable of its own. The doctor reports which proxy is in effect and probes whether it is still reachable, because a configured-but-dead proxy fails every source at once.
